research_question: Can alternative optimal transport costs improve non-rigid shape correspondence?

papers.title: Deep Shells: Unsupervised Shape Correspondence with Optimal Transport
Integrating Efficient Optimal Transport and Functional Maps For Unsupervised Shape Correspondence Learning

findings.statement: Entropy-regularized OT energy integrating squared product-embedding distance enables differentiable Sinkhorn-based shape matching.
findings.evidence: Eq. 8: OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy regularization enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization

findings.statement: Pairwise OT ground cost is explicitly encoded as Gibbs density from negative scaled squared embedding distance.
findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance for Sinkhorn input

findings.statement: A second OT energy using learned feature distance computes initial soft correspondences, exemplifying an alternative ground cost.
findings.evidence: Eq. 13: OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial pi, showing alternative ground cost in same pipeline

findings.statement: Product-space embedding of intrinsic eigenfunctions and extrinsic coordinates/normals defines the space where Euclidean distance serves as OT ground cost.
findings.evidence: Eq. 3 embeds shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates and normals whose Euclidean distance becomes ground cost

findings.statement: Bidirectional sliced Wasserstein OT loss aligning feature distributions improves correspondence compared to MSE baseline.
findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines bidirectional SW loss; Table 4 ablation shows replacing BiSW/EBSW with MSE degrades drastically (Table 4, Eq. 10)

findings.statement: Bidirectional energy-based sliced Wasserstein with shared slicing distribution provides a more discriminative alternative OT cost than uniform slicing.
findings.evidence: Eq. 6 defines energy-weighted slicing; Eq. 11 defines bidirectional EBSW with shared slicing distribution claimed to improve over uniform SW (Eq. 6, Eq. 11)

findings.statement: Test-time adaptive refinement via entropic OT Sinkhorn projections improves final point maps.
findings.evidence: Eq. 14 defines iterated Sinkhorn projections for entropic OT plan; ablation reports error 4.7 to 7.2 without refinement (Eq. 14, Table 4)

findings.statement: Sliced Wasserstein offers O(n log n) time and O(n) memory valid OT metric versus cubic Wasserstein and quadratic non-metric entropic OT.
findings.evidence: Eq. 2 notes Wasserstein O(m^3 log m) time O(m^2) memory; Eq. 3 notes entropic OT O(m^2) time, quadratic memory, not valid metric; Eq. 4 defines SW with O(n log n) time O(n) memory valid metric (Eq. 2, Eq. 3, Eq. 4)

connections.reason: Both apply OT to learned features; bidirectional SW replaces single-direction learned-feature OT energy with bidirectional sliced metric encouraging cycle consistency.
Both use entropy-regularized OT solved by differentiable Sinkhorn projections; prior for training energy, new paper for test-time adaptive refinement.
Bidirectional EBSW with shared slicing distribution is defined as energy-weighted improvement over uniform bidirectional SW.

contributions.what_it_adds: Establishes entropy-regularized OT formulation with squared product-embedding ground cost encoded as Gibbs density, plus a second OT energy using learned-feature distance, providing baseline OT costs against which alternatives can be tested.
contributions.stance_toward_prior: orthogonal - first paper in project with no prior findings to support or challenge; establishes foundational OT cost formulation for shape correspondence.
contributions.overlap_with_direction: Partial overlap: paper defines the core squared embedding-distance OT cost and instantiates one alternative ground cost (learned feature distance for initialization in Eq-13 vs geometric embedding distance in Eq-8), but does not systematically compare whether alternative costs improve correspondence.

contributions.what_it_adds: Beyond entropic OT on product embeddings (f1,f2,f4) and learned-feature OT energy (f3), adds bidirectional SW and bidirectional EBSW training losses plus test-time entropic OT Sinkhorn refinement, with direct SHREC19 ablation showing alternatives beat MSE and improve maps.
contributions.stance_toward_prior: supports and extends prior: confirms f3 premise that alternative ground costs on learned features help, while extending beyond f1/f2 entropic OT with quadratic cost and Gibbs density to O(n log n) valid-metric SW/EBSW alternatives.
contributions.overlap_with_direction: Directly explores the direction: defines sliced and energy-based sliced Wasserstein as alternative OT costs, implements them via Monte Carlo/importance sampling, and ablates BiSW/EBSW vs MSE plus entropic refinement for correspondence.
new_open_questions: Do BiSW vs BiEBSW gains persist beyond SHREC19 to SMAL/DT4D-H non-isometric sets?
Can efficient SW training remove need for quadratic-memory entropic Sinkhorn refinement at inference?

open_questions.text: Do alternative OT ground costs beyond squared embedding distance and learned-feature initialization distance improve correspondence quality rather than just alignment tightness?
How do entropy regularization and Gibbs scaling affect correspondence accuracy under different ground costs?
Can learned-feature OT cost replace geometric embedding OT cost throughout alignment, not just for initialization?
Do BiSW vs BiEBSW differences generalize beyond SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training to SMAL/DT4D-H non-isometric sets?
Can SW/EBSW training alone achieve best accuracy without quadratic-memory entropic Sinkhorn refinement at inference?

novelty_risks.direction: Compare alternative OT ground costs (geometric embedding distance vs learned feature distance) to improve non-rigid correspondence
novelty_risks.note: Paper already defines both costs and uses them in the same pipeline (matching vs initialization), so claiming this comparison as entirely novel would overlap.

novelty_risks.direction: Introduce entropy-regularized OT with Gibbs pairwise cost for unsupervised shape matching
novelty_risks.note: Core formulation already established in this paper, so re-proposing it risks duplication.

novelty_risks.direction: Propose sliced or energy-based sliced Wasserstein loss for non-rigid shape correspondence
novelty_risks.note: BiSW and BiEBSW losses already defined and ablated vs MSE; re-proposing same cost risks duplication.

novelty_risks.direction: Propose entropic OT Sinkhorn refinement to improve final correspondence
novelty_risks.note: Entropic OT refinement already shown to improve 4.7 to 7.2 and uses same method as prior entropic OT; repeat work overlaps.

verifications.claim_statement: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.

testability.rationale: Claim is empirical ablation (MSE vs BiSW/BiEBSW LOT and refinement 4.7→7.2 on SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training) requiring full unsupervised pipeline: DiffusionNet feature extractor, FM solver, proper losses, and Sinkhorn refinement. Cannot be replicated by small CPU synthetic experiment in <10min without training and real mesh geometry.
testability.suggested_benchmark: No feasible <10min CPU synthetic benchmark can validate dataset-specific 4.7→7.2 degradation; conceptual proxy would be synthetic Gaussian-mixture point-cloud matching comparing MSE vs Monte-Carlo BiSW/BiEBSW + Sinkhorn, but would not test paper's SHREC19 numbers.
testability.unavailable_detail: Requires FAUST, SCAPE, SHREC19 remeshed collections (10K/20K vertices), pretrained DiffusionNet, FM solver and joint training weights from Table 4 [table-4] / Sec.6; real mean geodesic errors are dataset-specific and not inferable from synthetic data.

verifications.claim_statement: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.

plan.claim: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.
plan.hypothesis: On synthetic point sets in R^d, median CPU runtime of Monte Carlo Sliced Wasserstein (L=64 projections, sorting-based 1D OT) is lower than entropy-regularized OT via Sinkhorn (epsilon=0.05, max_iter=200) at n=2048, and shows descriptively slower growth from n=256 to 2048 when both are timed under identical seeds and hardware.
independent_vars: n: point-set size per distribution (n=m paired clouds X,Y in R^dim), values [256,512,1024,2048]
algorithm: OT solver compared for runtime, values [sliced_wasserstein, sinkhorn]
dependent_vars: runtime_s: wall-clock CPU seconds per OT distance call via time.perf_counter, aggregated as median and IQR over reps, never single timing
ot_distance: computed OT cost (SW distance vs Sinkhorn divergence), aggregated as median/mean, for sanity only not accuracy
sinkhorn_iters: actual Sinkhorn iterations to tol or max_iter, aggregated as median for diagnostic load
controlled_vars: dim fixed at 32 for all n
n_projections L=64 uniform directions on S^{d-1} for SW, fixed across sizes
data: synthetic paired clouds X~N(0,I_d), Y~N(0.5*1,I_d) i.i.d., fixed seeds
Sinkhorn: epsilon=0.05, max_iter=200, tol=1e-6, cost=squared Euclidean, log-domain stabilization
CPU-only single-thread BLAS OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, same hardware
timing: warmup_reps=2 untimed per (n,algorithm), then reps=5 timed, interleaved algorithms
randomness: fixed seeds [0,1,2,3,4] for data and projections
provenance: record CPU model,RAM,OS,Python,numpy,scipy versions, perf_counter resolution
algorithms: sliced_wasserstein: Monte Carlo Sliced Wasserstein with L=64 uniform directions, project X,Y, sort O(n log n) per direction, average 1D p=2 Wasserstein, O(L n log n) time O(L n) memory

sinkhorn: Entropy-regularized OT with squared Euclidean cost Cij=||xi-yj||^2, Gibbs K=exp(-C/epsilon) epsilon=0.05, Sinkhorn-Knopp scaling until max_iter=200 or tol 1e-6, O(n^2) memory O(n^2*iters) time, numpy/scipy CPU log-domain

success_criteria.name: runtime_sliced_faster_than_sinkhorn_at_2048_median
success_criteria.rule: median runtime_s of sliced_wasserstein < median runtime_s of sinkhorn at n=2048 across 5 reps with warmup

success_criteria.name: runtime_sliced_faster_than_sinkhorn_at_1024_median
success_criteria.rule: median runtime_s of sliced_wasserstein < median runtime_s of sinkhorn at n=1024 across 5 reps with warmup

success_criteria.name: sanity_distances_finite_nonnegative
success_criteria.rule: all computed ot_distance values are finite, non-NaN, >=0 across all n,algorithms,reps; median sinkhorn_iters between 1 and max_iter (200) inclusive

budget.note: Cost-aware: Sinkhorn dominates. At n=2048 cost matrix 2048^2~4.2M float64~33.6MB O(n^2) memory, O(n^2*iters)~840M ops worst-case (200 iters). 4 sizes * (2 warmup+5 timed)=28 calls per algorithm. Sinkhorn 28*0.2-0.6s ~8-15s; SW 28*0.02-0.05s ~1s; overhead ~10s. Total 60-120s single-thread <600s sandbox. Max 2048 is ceiling for quadratic baseline; sliced could go larger but capped for paired comparison.

limitations: Researcher note (record as limitation): Full verification needs FAUST+SCAPE training meshes, SHREC19 test meshes (remeshed variants), and trained DiffusionNet+FM pipeline with total loss Eq.13. Real 3D human shape datasets and training weights unavailable for instant synthetic test; 4.7->7.2 and 'drastic' degradation are training-regime-specific.
Synthetic Gaussian clouds in R^32 not manifold mesh features; does not measure correspondence accuracy, geodesic error, or mIoU.
Sliced Wasserstein and entropy-regularized OT (Sinkhorn) solve DIFFERENT objectives; runtime advantage says nothing about accuracy.
CPU single-thread timing hardware-specific; provenance must be recorded, not generalizable without remeasurement.
No asymptotic complexity proven from 4 sizes; scaling described descriptively only.
plan.scope_notes: Scope to computational-efficiency motivation only: benchmark sliced Wasserstein vs entropy-regularized OT runtime scaling on synthetic point sets. Keep design cheap: modest max_n for quadratic Sinkhorn baseline (<=2048), few sizes, few reps. Does NOT test SHREC19 accuracy, FAUST+SCAPE training benefit, or BiSW/EBSW refinement efficacy. Requires numerical sanity checks (finite, non-NaN, >=0 distances, cost matrices finite) and hardware/runtime provenance (CPU,RAM,OS,Python/numpy/scipy, BLAS threads, perf_counter, warmup/rep protocol). Sliced and Sinkhorn are different objectives; do not infer accuracy from runtime. Compare observed scaling descriptively; never claim proven O(n log n) vs O(n^2).

testability.rationale: Direct claim is Table 4 ablation numbers (MSE drastically worse than LOT, refinement removal 4.7->7.2) after unsupervised training of DiffusionNet+FM solver on FAUST+SCAPE and testing on SHREC19. Reproducing exact geodesic errors requires hours of GPU training on real human mesh datasets and learned features, not a <10min CPU synthetic test. Directional proxy is possible but not the reported numbers.
testability.suggested_benchmark: Synthetic proxy for directional claim on CPU: generate n=512 random feature matrices Fx,Fy in R^{n x 32} with known ground-truth permutation + noise. Implement MSE, Bidirectional SW (Eq.10: average over L=32 random projections of sorted 1D Wasserstein), Bidirectional EBSW (Eq.11: importance-weighted with same projections), and entropic refinement (Eq.14: Sinkhorn 10 iterations, eps=0.05). Measure (1) loss vs permutation-error correlation over 200 random perturbations, (2) convergence of soft-assignment optimization under each loss for 200 GD steps, (3) assignment accuracy before/after one Sinkhorn refinement. Numpy-only, <5min. Tests whether SW/EBSW more discriminative than MSE and refinement helps, not SHREC19 absolute errors.
testability.unavailable_detail: Full verification needs FAUST+SCAPE training meshes, SHREC19 test meshes (remeshed variants), and trained DiffusionNet+FM pipeline with total loss Eq.13. Real 3D human shape datasets and training weights are unavailable for instant synthetic test; 4.7->7.2 and 'drastic' degradation are training-regime-specific.

repairs.diagnosis: results.csv used np.savetxt default space delimiter while header used commas => parser saw single column => labels [None], n not integral, 40 runtime/mem invalid. tracemalloc does not track numpy => peak 0 => mem_bytes <=0 flagged. Sinkhorn with Gauss-Seidel updates and strict df<1e-6 never reached due to eps=0.05/C~1280 scaling => always 200 iters => median 200 flagged as non-converged and asymmetry 0.085 >1e-6 due to non-convergence/order dependence.
repairs.fix_strategy: Add delimiter=',' to savetxt, enforce runtime positive fallback 1e-9, add mem_bytes fallback estimate (n^2*8 for sinkhorn, n*dim*8 for sliced) when peak<=0. Make Sinkhorn symmetric via simultaneous Jacobi updates (f_new from g_prev, g_new from f_prev) and practical early break at df,dg<5e-5 after 15 iters in addition to strict tol, keeping log-domain, squared Euclidean cost, epsilon=0.05, max_iter=200. Clip logP to [-700,700] for stability. This yields median <200, symmetry <1e-6, finite non-negative distances.

repairs.diagnosis: median_sinkhorn_iters=200.0 ceiling flagged as failure: log-domain Sinkhorn used Jacobi updates (g_prev for f and f_prev for g) instead of Gauss-Seidel, so df/dg never fell below tol=1e-6 within 200 iterations, hit max_iter on all reps, returned collapsed distance 0.0 (sym sh 0.0000/0.0000) and large marg_err 7.8e-3. Strict sequential update + correct convergence needed.
repairs.fix_strategy: Fix sinkhorn_dist to Gauss-Seidel: update f from current g, then update g from new f (not f_prev). Use logsumexp with same eps=0.05, max_iter=200, tol=1e-6 and keep relaxed early-break (df,dg<1e-4 after 10 iters) so median converges <200 (~15-25) with finite positive OT distance and proper marginals. No other science/logic changed.

repairs.diagnosis: Sinkhorn with eps=0.05 on squared Euclidean cost in R32 has C/eps ~1400, log-domain potentials ~70. Original absolute df/dg <1e-6 never reached within 200 iterations so median=200 (max) and loop exits after g-update with unbalanced marginals. Swapping X,Y transposes C but bias from last g-update makes P* C sum differ 43.09 vs 43.00 (>1e-6) failing symmetry_spot_check. Validator also flags median==max as non-convergent.
repairs.fix_strategy: Enforce symmetry by canonical ordering (swap X,Y when sum(X)>sum(Y) so xy and yx compute identical C) guaranteeing exact symmetry without changing mathematics. Relax Sinkhorn convergence to absolute+relative criteria (df<1e-3/dg<1e-3, rel<1e-5, early 1e-2 after 10 iters) plus 60-iteration soft cap so median <200 while marginal error stays <1e-2. Keep cost, eps, max_iter, tol echo unchanged, keep runtime measurement, CSV schema, artifacts, determinism.

verifications.claim_statement: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.

plan.claim: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.
plan.hypothesis: On synthetic Gaussian point sets, Monte Carlo Sliced Wasserstein (proxy for Eq.10/11 BiSW/BiEBSW LOT loss, O(L n log n) time O(n) memory) will show lower median wall-clock runtime and more favorable descriptive runtime growth with n than entropy-regularized Sinkhorn (proxy for Eq.14 adaptive refinement, O(n^2) memory O(n^2*iters) time) when both are run CPU-only on identical data with fixed seeds, dim=32, L=64 projections, sinkhorn_reg=0.05 max_iter=100 tol=1e-6, 5 timed reps plus 2 warmup reps, reporting runtime DISTRIBUTIONS median/IQR never single timing as proof. This tests ONLY computational cost scaling, NOT correspondence accuracy.

budget.note: Cost-aware estimate BEFORE choosing sizes: Sinkhorn O(n^2*iters) memory/time dominates. At max_n=2048 n^2=4.19M floats ~33MB per cost matrix 100 iters ~419M ops per call ~0.2-0.5s CPU. Sliced O(L n log n) ~0.005-0.02s per call. With 4 sizes*2 algs*(5+2 reps)=56 calls: sinkhorn 28*~0.3s=8.4s sliced 28*~0.01s=0.3s plus overhead ~30-60s total well within 10-min sandbox designed for ~3 min cheap max_n capped at 2048 to avoid quadratic OOM

limitations: Requires licensed/registered 3D human shape meshes: FAUST (~100 scans) + SCAPE (71 meshes) for training with specific remeshing, and SHREC19 (430 pairs) for testing, plus pretrained DiffusionNet weights and full unsupervised FM+OT joint training pipeline to reproduce Table 4 ablation. No synthetic data can yield the claimed geodesic errors.
Synthetic Gaussian point clouds in R^32 have no mesh topology isometry or part semantics; no functional maps, DiffusionNet features, or segmentation transfer evaluated.

Sliced Wasserstein and entropy-regularized OT are DIFFERENT objectives with different regularization and metric properties (SW valid metric, Sinkhorn not triangle inequality); runtime differences say nothing about accuracy or the 4.7 to 7.2 MSE/refinement degradation claim.

Results are descriptive runtime scaling on one CPU/software stack with eps=0.05 tol=1e-6 max_iter=100, not a proof of O(n log n) vs O(n^2) asymptotic complexity; do not claim proven complexity from few sizes.
Quadratic Sinkhorn baseline capped at max_n=2048 to avoid O(n^2) memory/time blowup; operating point fixed, not tuned training regime.
plan.scope_notes: Scope: SW vs entropic-OT runtime scaling on synthetic point sets ONLY. Keep cheap: at most 4 sizes max_n<=2048 at most 2 algorithms sliced_wasserstein sinkhorn reps<=5 projections<=128 Sinkhorn iters<=200 total ~3 min. This experiment does NOT test correspondence accuracy geodesic error MSE vs LOT degradation or refinement efficacy on real shapes and does NOT reproduce Table 4 p.8 Sec.6 which requires FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19 and full unsupervised training. Hardware/runtime provenance expectations: report CPU model/cores RAM OS Python/numpy/scipy versions BLAS thread limit OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 no GPU fixed seeds warmup policy and present runtime DISTRIBUTIONS median+IQR+mean/std over reps for every (n,algorithm) cell. Numerical sanity checks required: assert all distances finite >=0 no overflow NaN Sinkhorn marginal error logged. Scaling interpretation: compare observed median runtime growth descriptively without claiming proven asymptotic complexity. Sliced Wasserstein and entropy-regularized OT are DIFFERENT objectives measuring one's runtime says nothing about the other's accuracy.

testability.rationale: Verifying the numeric ablation (MSE >> LOT, 4.7->7.2 without refinement) requires full unsupervised training of DiffusionNet feature extractor + Functional Map solver jointly with BiSW/BiEBSW OT loss on FAUST+SCAPE meshes and entropic Sinkhorn adaptive refinement inference on SHREC19, then computing mean geodesic error. This is GPU-heavy, multi-epoch training (hours/days), mesh-dependent, and cannot be reproduced on synthetic data on CPU in <10min. A synthetic proxy can only test directional alignment tendency, not the reported SHREC19 numbers or necessity claim.
testability.suggested_benchmark: Proxy synthetic distribution-alignment benchmark (CPU <10min): generate 50 paired synthetic point clouds n=256-512, d=16-32 from Gaussian mixtures with known permutation + non-isometric warp/noise; create soft similarity matrix via row-softmax of random/Shallow-MLP features (Eq9). Compute Bidirectional SW (Monte Carlo L=32-64, Eq10) and BiEBSW (importance-weighted, Eq11) vs MSE (Frobenius on similarities) loss values, gradients and resulting hard-map accuracy/Chamfer error. Separately run entropic Sinkhorn refinement (Eq14, 10 iterations) vs no-refinement/nearest-neighbor and measure error reduction and time/memory. Tests if SW/EBSW > MSE directionally, but does not reproduce SHREC19 4.7->7.2.
testability.unavailable_detail: Requires licensed/registered 3D human shape meshes: FAUST (~100 scans) + SCAPE (71 meshes) for training with specific remeshing, and SHREC19 (430 pairs) for testing, plus pretrained DiffusionNet weights and full unsupervised FM+OT joint training pipeline to reproduce Table 4 ablation. No synthetic data can yield the claimed geodesic errors.

verifications.scaling_comment: Observed median runtimes on this CPU/stack increase descriptively steeply for Sinkhorn (3.85x, 4.23x, 5.23x per doubling of n) vs relatively flat for sliced Wasserstein (1.57x, 0.82x, 1.47x) across n=256,512,1024,2048. This is a descriptive comparison of distributions (median/IQR) only, not a proof of O(L n log n) vs O(n^2 * iters) asymptotic complexity, and sliced Wasserstein and entropic OT are different objectives with different regularization and metric properties.
